9-panel cinematic storyboard CONTACT SHEET derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene.

Layout: a rigid 3x3 grid of 9 equal rectangular cells in a 16:9 landscape image. Each cell is exactly 1/3 of the width and 1/3 of the height. Separate cells with a thin black gutter.
- Content must not cross, bleed, or overlap a gutter. No collage.
- Each cell is a complete, independently framed shot — not a crop of a larger scene.

Scene: Tight editorial close-up push-in on SCARLETT VEGA (Image 2) wearing a fitted black cotton turtleneck with sleeves pushed to the elbows, small gold hoop earrings, a thin silver ring on her right index finger, caught mid-gesture as she drags the flat of her hand back from her mouth, wrist still angled up near her jaw, eyes flicking down toward that hand for a split second before the smirk lands, chin tilting toward the lens, breath held, shoulders squared and tense with post-punchline adrenaline. She stands on a comedy club stage, the chrome mic head just clipping into the bottom corner of the frame slightly out of focus, the warm red-brown brick back wall collapsed into deep velvet blackness behind her with only the faintest mortar texture catching a sliver of spill, a suggestion of a vertical mic stand shaft and a dark curtain edge dissolving into bokeh, dust motes drifting through the beam. Hard single front spotlight plus a punchy direct on-camera flash quality: hot specular highlights on damp skin, a bead of sweat glinting at her temple, crisp clean shadow edge under her jaw and cheekbone, glossy coral mouth reading as the single saturated accent against an otherwise black and neutral frame, highlights slightly warm, shadows dropping fast to true black with no diffusion. Shot at eye level, 85mm portrait lens wide open, extremely shallow depth of field so only her eyes and mouth are razor sharp, subtle handheld micro-movement, clean true-to-life color grading with crisp whites and warm natural skin.

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
Image 1 (primary): Primary source scene — generate 9 variant shots from this image
